cases.sentence: По моему мнению, действовать на ___ может только тот, который имеет высшее развитие, который…
cases.explain: «другой народ» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “It seems to me,” Alexey Alexandrovitch said languidly, and with no haste, “that that’s the same thing. In my opinion, influence over another people is only possible to the people which has the higher development, which. …”

cases.sentence: Мы видим, что Рейн офранцузился, а немцы не ниже стоят! – кричал он. – Тут есть ___!
cases.explain: «другой закон» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But that’s just the question,” Pestsov broke in in his bass. He was always in a hurry to speak, and seemed always to put his whole soul into what he was saying. “In what are we to make higher development consist? The English, the French, the Germans, which is at the highest stage of development? Which of them will nationalize the other? We see the Rhine provinces have been turned French, but the Germans are not at a lower stage!” he shouted. “There is another law at work there.”

cases.sentence: – Мне кажется, что влияние всегда на стороне ___, – сказал Алексей Александрович, слегка поднимая брови.
cases.explain: «истинного образования» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I fancy that the greater influence is always on the side of true civilization,” said Alexey Alexandrovitch, slightly lifting his eyebrows.

cases.sentence: – Но в чем же мы должны полагать признаки ___? – сказал Песцов.
cases.explain: «истинного образования» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “But what are we to lay down as the outward signs of true civilization?” said Pestsov.

cases.sentence: Я не вижу ___, почему классическим наукам дано преимущество пред реальными.
cases.explain: «ясных доводов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “I am not expressing my own opinion of either form of culture,” Sergey Ivanovitch said, holding out his glass with a smile of condescension, as to a child. “I only say that both sides have strong arguments to support them,” he went on, addressing Alexey Alexandrovitch. “My sympathies are classical from education, but in this discussion I am personally unable to arrive at a conclusion. I see no distinct grounds for classical studies being given a preeminence over scientific studies.”

cases.sentence: Я не вижу ясных доводов, почему ___ дано преимущество пред реальными.
cases.explain: «классическим наукам» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “I am not expressing my own opinion of either form of culture,” Sergey Ivanovitch said, holding out his glass with a smile of condescension, as to a child. “I only say that both sides have strong arguments to support them,” he went on, addressing Alexey Alexandrovitch. “My sympathies are classical from education, but in this discussion I am personally unable to arrive at a conclusion. I see no distinct grounds for classical studies being given a preeminence over scientific studies.”

cases.sentence: – Естественные имеют столь же педагогически-развивательное влияние, – подхватил Песков. – Возьмите одну астрономию, возьмите ботанику, зоологию с ее системой ___!
cases.explain: «общих законов» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “The natural sciences have just as great an educational value,” put in Pestsov. “Take astronomy, take botany, or zoology with its system of general principles.”

cases.sentence: – Я не могу вполне с этим согласиться, – отвечал Алексей Александрович. – Мне кажется, что нельзя не признать того, что ___ изучения форм языков особенно благотворно действует на духовное развитие.
cases.explain: «самый процесс» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I cannot quite agree with that,” responded Alexey Alexandrovitch. “It seems to me that one must admit that the very process of studying the forms of language has a peculiarly favorable influence on intellectual development. Moreover, it cannot be denied that the influence of the classical authors is in the highest degree moral, while, unfortunately, with the study of the natural sciences are associated the false and noxious doctrines which are the curse of our day.”

cases.sentence: Сергей Иванович хотел что-то сказать, но Песцов своим ___ перебил его.
cases.explain: «густым басом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Sergey Ivanovitch would have said something, but Pestsov interrupted him in his rich bass. He began warmly contesting the justice of this view. Sergey Ivanovitch waited serenely to speak, obviously with a convincing reply ready.

cases.sentence: Сергей Иванович спокойно дожидался слова, очевидно с готовым ___.
cases.explain: «победительным возражением» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Sergey Ivanovitch would have said something, but Pestsov interrupted him in his rich bass. He began warmly contesting the justice of this view. Sergey Ivanovitch waited serenely to speak, obviously with a convincing reply ready.

cases.sentence: Но теперь мы знаем, что в этих пилюлях ___ лежит целебная сила антинигилизма, и мы смело предлагаем их нашим пациентам…
cases.explain: «классического образования» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “If it had not been for the distinctive property of anti-nihilistic influence on the side of classical studies, we should have considered the subject more, have weighed the arguments on both sides,” said Sergey Ivanovitch with a subtle smile, “we should have given elbow-room to both tendencies. But now we know that these little pills of classical learning possess the medicinal property of anti-nihilism, and we boldly prescribe them to our patients. … But what if they had no such medicinal property?” he wound up humorously.

cases.sentence: Но теперь мы знаем, что в этих пилюлях классического образования лежит ___ антинигилизма, и мы смело предлагаем их нашим пациентам…
cases.explain: «целебная сила» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “If it had not been for the distinctive property of anti-nihilistic influence on the side of classical studies, we should have considered the subject more, have weighed the arguments on both sides,” said Sergey Ivanovitch with a subtle smile, “we should have given elbow-room to both tendencies. But now we know that these little pills of classical learning possess the medicinal property of anti-nihilism, and we boldly prescribe them to our patients. … But what if they had no such medicinal property?” he wound up humorously.

cases.sentence: Правительство, очевидно, руководствуется ___, оставаясь индифферентным к влияниям, которые могут иметь принимаемые меры.
cases.explain: «общими соображениями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I can’t agree even,” said he, “that the government had that aim. The government obviously is guided by abstract considerations, and remains indifferent to the influence its measures may exercise. The education of women, for instance, would naturally be regarded as likely to be harmful, but the government opens schools and universities for women.”

cases.sentence: Например, вопрос ___ должен бы был считаться зловредным, но правительство открывает женские курсы и университеты.
cases.explain: «женского образования» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

The government obviously is guided by abstract considerations, and remains indifferent to the influence its measures may exercise. The education of women, for instance, would naturally be regarded as likely to be harmful, but the government opens schools and universities for women.”

cases.sentence: Например, вопрос женского образования должен бы был считаться зловредным, но правительство открывает ___ и университеты.

cases.translation: “I can’t agree even,” said he, “that the government had that aim. The government obviously is guided by abstract considerations, and remains indifferent to the influence its measures may exercise. The education of women, for instance, would naturally be regarded as likely to be harmful, but the government opens schools and universities for women.”

cases.sentence: И разговор тотчас же перескочил на новую тему ___.
cases.explain: «женского образования» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: And the conversation at once passed to the new subject of the education of women.

cases.sentence: – Я, напротив, полагаю, что эти два вопроса неразрывно связаны, – сказал Песцов, – это ___.
cases.explain: «ложный круг» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I consider, on the contrary, that the two questions are inseparably connected together,” said Pestsov; “it is a vicious circle. Woman is deprived of rights from lack of education, and the lack of education results from the absence of rights. We must not forget that the subjection of women is so complete, and dates from such ages back that we are often unwilling to recognize the gulf that separates them from us,” said he.

cases.sentence: – Но если женщины, как ___, и могут занимать эти места, то, мне кажется, вы неправильно употребили выражение «правá«.
cases.explain: «редкое исключение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “But if women, as a rare exception, can occupy such positions, it seems to me you are wrong in using the expression ‘rights.’ It would be more correct to say duties. Every man will agree that in doing the duty of a juryman, a witness, a telegraph clerk, we feel we are performing duties. And therefore it would be correct to say that women are seeking duties, and quite legitimately. And one can but sympathize with this desire to assist in the general labor of man.”

cases.sentence: Всякий согласится, что, исполняя какую-нибудь должность присяжного, гласного, ___, мы чувствуем, что исполняем обязанность.
cases.explain: «телеграфного чиновника» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “But if women, as a rare exception, can occupy such positions, it seems to me you are wrong in using the expression ‘rights.’ It would be more correct to say duties. Every man will agree that in doing the duty of a juryman, a witness, a telegraph clerk, we feel we are performing duties. And therefore it would be correct to say that women are seeking duties, and quite legitimately. And one can but sympathize with this desire to assist in the general labor of man.”

cases.sentence: И можно только сочувствовать этому их желанию помочь общему ___.
cases.explain: «мужскому труду» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.

Every man will agree that in doing the duty of a juryman, a witness, a telegraph clerk, we feel we are performing duties. And therefore it would be correct to say that women are seeking duties, and quite legitimately. And one can but sympathize with this desire to assist in the general labor of man.”

cases.sentence: – А пословица? – сказал князь, давно уж прислушиваясь к разговору и блестя своими маленькими ___, – при дочерях можно: – волос долог…
cases.explain: «насмешливыми глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “How about the proverb?” said the prince, who had a long while been intent on the conversation, his little comical eyes twinkling. “I can say it before my daughter: her hair is long, because her wit is. …”

cases.sentence: – Все равно, что я бы искал права быть кормилицей и обижался бы, что женщинам платят, а мне не хотят, – сказал ___.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Just as though I should seek the right to be a wet-nurse and feel injured because women are paid for the work, while no one will take me,” said the old prince.

cases.sentence: Туровцын разразился ___, и Сергей Иванович пожалел, что не он сказал это.
cases.explain: «громким смехом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Turovtsin exploded in a loud roar of laughter and Sergey Ivanovitch regretted that he had not made this comparison. Even Alexey Alexandrovitch smiled.

cases.sentence: – Нет, англичанин выкормил на корабле своего ребенка, – сказал ___, позволяя себе эту вольность разговора при своих дочерях.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No, there was an Englishman who did suckle his baby on board ship,” said the old prince, feeling this freedom in conversation permissible before his own daughters.

cases.sentence: – Но мы стоим за принцип, за идеал! – ___ возражал Песцов. – Женщина хочет иметь право быть независимою, образованною.
cases.explain: «звучным басом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “But we take our stand on principle as the ideal,” replied Pestsov in his mellow bass. “Woman desires to have rights, to be independent, educated. She is oppressed, humiliated by the consciousness of her disabilities.”

cases.sentence: – А я стеснен и подавлен тем, что меня не примут в кормилицы в ___, – опять сказал старый князь, к великой радости Туровцына, со смеху уронившего спаржу толстым концом в соус.
cases.explain: «воспитательный дом» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “And I’m oppressed and humiliated that they won’t engage me at the Foundling,” the old prince said again, to the huge delight of Turovtsin, who in his mirth dropped his asparagus with the thick end in the sauce.
